title: A Non-Iterative Phase Retrieval Method for Defocused, Coarsely Scanned 4D-STEM Data
content: Tilt-corrected brightfield scanning transmission electron microscopy (tcBF-STEM) is a phase contrast imaging technique that uses a defocused four dimensional STEM (4D-STEM) dataset to reconstruct high resolution images which has recently been explored for efficient low-dose imaging of biological samples. Compared to conventional transmission electron microscopy (CTEM) imaging, tcBF-STEM is relatively insensitive to inelastic scattering as the inelastic scattering angles are generally small and the contribution of the chromatic aberration of the post-specimen optics is greatly diminished in STEM mode. This has made the method particularly attractive for imaging of thick sections, where it has been demonstrated to have double the contrast compared to energy filtered CTEM when imaging 550 nm thick vitrified samples [1].
